newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude flat, Asian demand lifts W. Africa.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude flat, Asian demand lifts W. Africa.

text.p: North Sea crudes struggled to make significant headway on Thursday amid slack early May refinery demand, but West African grades drew support from Asian interest, traders said.
June Brent shed eight cents to $17.73 a barrel by 1207 GMT, extending Wednesday's losses sparked by rising stocks and a sloppy gasoline market in the United States.

The June/July intermonth spread traded at -19 cents, in line with late Wednesday's levels and Brent Contracts for Difference were equally flat, changing hands at June Brent -59 and -60 cents, dealers said.

North Sea Forties edged a couple of cents higher to Dated Brent +6/+10 cents as more early May barrels were placed in private trade on Wednesday. But other grades were pinned back as northwest European refineries remained relaxed.
"We're still working out what we need for our own system and what we will be offering," said a trader for a major North Sea producer.
Dated Brent was valued around May Brent -45 cents, equivalent to June Brent -73 cents, in extremely thin talk.
One Brent cargo was nominated May 2-4 loading dates after deferral requests for clocked May 1-3 cargoes were turned down.
West African markets were quiet after a flurry of activity earlier in the week but the mood was cautiously bullish, traders said.
Bonny Light and Qua Iboe (BQ) were talked at Dated Brent +30 cents, Brass River at Brent +35 cents to +40 cents and Forcados at Dated Brent -20 cents, they said.
Asian refiners picked up Nigerian Bonny Light/Medium, Forcados and Angolan Palanca on Tuesday or Wednesday.
In a quiet Mediterranean market, Russian Urals was steady at around Dated Brent -$1.15/-$1.10 a barrel but some traders said the discount could widen as May approaches.

"(Urals) prices are strong in the -$1.10 to -$1.15 range. I think this will slowly start to dwindle away as we get closer to May because in May there will be alternative crudes to choose from like Syrian and Kirkuk," one refiner said.
Traders said no agreement has been reached yet on Syrian crude term prices for May in talks between Syrian state oil company Sytrol and term lifters.

There was, however, a consensus among buyers for a rollover of the April price of Dated Brent -95 cents for Syrian Light, as most were not prepared to accept Sytrol's initial offer of Brent -82 cents.
Syria asked Dated Brent -$4.60 for its Souedie grade.
"People would be satisfied with a rollover of the April prices to May...Everyone is bidding (Brent) -98 cents or -99 cents but will be satisfied with (Brent) -95 cents," a term lifter said.
